newsitem.title: JORDAN: Hamas urges U.S. to send political head to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Hamas urges U.S. to send political head to Jordan.

text.p: The new political head of the militant Islamic group Hamas welcomed reports on Thursday that his predecessor Mousa Abu Marzook may be set free from a New York jail to Jordan but said his release must be unconditional.
Khaled Meshal, elected head of the Hamas politburo after Abu Marzook's 1995 arrest in New York, said it would be unjust to keep him in detention.

"We think his release should take place without any preconditions," Meshal told Reuters. "Blackmail is not right because Dr Moussa's cause is a just cause, and there is no justification in continuing to detain him."

Israeli security sources confirmed on Thursday a newspaper report that Israeli, Jordanian and U.S. officials were secretly examining a deal to send Mousa Abu Marzook to Amman in return for a promise to shun violence.

Jordan expelled Abu Marzook, who said he was only involved in political activities in Amman, in June 1995. The move was aimed at improving ties with Israel and the Palestinian Authority. He was arrested in the United States a month later.

Israel alleged that as political leader of the Islamic militant group, he was responsible for attacks that killed scores of Israelis. It demanded his extradition. But Israeli newspapers said intelligence officials wanted him sent to Jordan for fear of a wave of Hamas attacks should he arrive in Israel.
"We are confident there are a lot of countries that would open their doors to Dr Mousa...and we are thankful for the steps that the Jordanian government are exerting," Meshal said.
Meshal said Abu Marzook would continue to play a "leading role" in Hamas if he was set free, but denied that any Hamas members in Jordan were involved in violence.
"The role which Hamas figures play in Jordan is...political and information issues only, the role in resisting the (Israeli) occupation...all that is inside occupied Palestine," he said.
"We hope he will be released quickly and return to practice his leading role inside Hamas for the benefit of the Palestinian people and the Palestinian cause."
Abu Marzook's lawyer said in New York on Thursday his client would have no problem signing a statement promising to shun violence.
Hamas has warned of guerrilla attacks should Abu Marzook be extradited to the Jewish state. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has asked the United States not to send him to Israel.
Suicide bombers from the military wing of Hamas, which rejects the Palestinian-Israeli self-rule deal as a sell-out, killed dozens of Israelis in a series of attacks one year ago.
Since then Hamas figures in the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip announced guidelines for peaceful opposition to the accord.
But Meshal denied any change in Hamas policy.
"When there is a lull in operations...this is due to circumstances in which the Mujahideen (holy fighters) in the military wing operates. It is tied to their circumstances on the ground," he said.
